hints: Focus on Group 2 going down from Mg to Ba, where atoms get bigger and the outer electrons are further from the nucleus.
Notice that this makes electrons easier to remove, so ionisation energy falls and the metals become stronger reducing agents.
Now recall the two opposite solubility trends for Group 2, hydroxides get more soluble down the group while sulfates get less soluble.
walkthrough:
**Place the elements in Group 2**

Magnesium to barium means going down Group 2. Atomic radius increases and shielding increases, so trends are very regular.

Trend idea:
$$\text{atomic size increases down the group}$$

**Check atomic and redox properties**

First ionisation energy decreases down the group because the outer $2s$ electrons are further away and less attracted. The metals also lose electrons more easily, so they are stronger reducing agents and weaker oxidising agents.

**Check the two solubility trends**

This is the classic pair to learn together. Hydroxides become more soluble down the group, from sparingly soluble $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ to fairly soluble $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$. Sulfates do the opposite and become less soluble, from soluble $\text{MgSO}_4$ to insoluble $\text{BaSO}_4$.

**Pick the property that increases**

Ionisation energy decreases, oxidising power decreases, sulfate solubility decreases. Only hydroxide solubility increases from magnesium to barium.

options.A: Incorrect. First ionisation energy decreases from Mg to Ba because atomic radius increases and shielding increases, so the outer electrons are held less strongly.
options.B: Incorrect. Oxidising power means gaining electrons, but Group 2 metals lose electrons. They become easier to oxidise down the group, so reducing power increases and oxidising power decreases.
options.C: Correct. The solubility of Group 2 hydroxides increases down the group. $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is sparingly soluble while $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is much more soluble, giving a more alkaline solution.
options.D: Incorrect. This is the opposite trend. Group 2 sulfate solubility decreases down the group, from soluble $\text{MgSO}_4$ to insoluble $\text{BaSO}_4$. Many students mix this up with the hydroxide trend.
